key_insight: This paper introduces interval and fuzzy physics-augmented neural networks that can learn constitutive laws while explicitly quantifying uncertainty. Instead of predicting a single stress response, the models produce bounded stress predictions that can enclose noisy or sparse experimental data.
problem_solved: Constitutive modeling often relies on limited, noisy, or heterogeneous stress–deformation data, making it hard to build reliable mechanics models and assess uncertainty. The paper addresses the need for models that are both physics-consistent and uncertainty-aware.
method: Train physics-augmented neural networks to learn hyperelastic free-energy density functions.
Use automatic differentiation to derive stresses from the learned energy branches.
Construct lower/mean/upper interval predictions (iPANN) and fuzzy representations (fPANN) to bound uncertainty in the constitutive response.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in scientific computing, this provides a principled way to combine data, physics, and uncertainty quantification in a single model. It is especially useful when experimental data are scarce and trustworthy extrapolation is critical.
visual_elements: A schematic showing input strain/deformation going into a physics-augmented neural network and outputting stress bounds.

paper_title: Interval and fuzzy physics-augmented neural networks (iPANN and fPANN) for uncertainty quantification and propagation in constitutive modeling
paper_authors: Somesh Pratap Singh, Govinda Anantha Padmanabha, Jingye Tan, Steven Yang, Reese E. Jones
